targets.text: associate hands back strict facts: every claim in the answer rests on a basis a reader can check, and a count comes with the command that produced it

in a recorded live worker run and a recorded live cortex run with the default contract, every item in the answer section of answer.md has a check kind, a cited call and a passed check, and no item appears there that check.json lists as failed
The operator and mesh peers who read an associate answer and act on it, and a reviewer who wants to run the basis of any claim in it again
a reader who was not part of the run takes three items from a recorded answer, runs the printed command or read in the pinned checkout, and gets the printed result for all three

In the 36 measured broad runs of the decider plan (worker, six repositories, 1,657 statements), an outside grader (Gemini, the main reading) graded 150 statements false: 133 in the model's unchecked text, 16 resting on a quote-found fact and 1 on a fact whose quote was refused. Two Claude graders with a third for disputes graded 71 false: 65 in unchecked text and 6 on a quote-found fact. The count depends on how strictly a list given as complete and a claim copied from a stale document are judged. No person graded. The attribution of a statement to a fact is by text matching, a heuristic
the numbers are recomputed from the stored t12 results after grading is settled with an outside model's verdicts, and the spec is corrected if they change
Every fact in the rendered answer is shown with how to check it: the command, search or read of the call it cites, as the walk recorded it, and that call's result, so a reader can run it again
a live worker run on a broad task hands back at least one count fact, and answer.md shows its command and result exactly as walk.jsonl and results/wN.txt hold them

The rendered answer is made only of items whose basis passed; an item that fails is dropped from the answer, the model is told which items were dropped and why and may answer again, and the model's unchecked text stays in the export and is not part of the answer
in a live run, no sentence of the model's summary or final message appears in the answer section of answer.md, and the export still holds both
The harness takes the command from the walk entry the fact cites (arguments as used), never from text the model retypes
a fact whose cited call ran a different command than the model describes renders the command from the walk; a node test covers it
For a fact that states a number, the harness checks that the number is in the saved result of the cited call, and reports or refuses the fact when it is not, by the model's check mode

the '604 test files' fact from the measured colleague run, replayed from its stored export, is reported: 604 is in the cited result, but the cited command counts entries; the replay shows what the check can and cannot catch

A fact the decider answers part or little is returned to the model once with that answer and the fix (narrow the value to what the evidence shows, or point at a source that shows the rest). If it comes back unchanged or is still answered part or little, it stays in the answer marked 'evidence shows part of the value', with the decider's answer beside it. A fact answered none is dropped and the model is told why. All within the existing retry rounds
a fact answered part is returned once, and the next finish either narrows the value or the fact is kept with the mark; the walk shows it

The broad report states, per run, how many graded statements rest on a passed basis and how many of those were graded false, with the matching done by the harness from item ids and not by text similarity
for the stored t12 runs the harness attribution and my text-matching attribution are compared and the differences listed

On the six broad tasks, 3 runs per arm, statements in the rendered answer graded false are 0 for counts whose command is shown, and the strict arm has fewer statements graded false than the present arm in at least 5 of 6 repositories under the committed broad rule
the comparison is graded blind by graders that include at least one outside model or a person, since all three graders so far are Claude models
No change to lobes-cli or colleague; gate.json stays version 9; the quote-found count and the new counts are never called accuracy
the wording test over docs finds no use of accuracy or score for these counts, and git diff shows no change under lobes-cli, colleague or gate.json
The harness does not run a model-chosen command a second time in this work; re-running is left to the reader or a later spec
a node test shows that checking a hand-back starts no process and makes no tool call: it reads the walk and the saved results only

Each fact states its kind of check: 'direct' (the cited call's result shows it: a quote or a number), 'llm' (a judgement the decider or a model must make, named as such in the answer), or 'derived' (it follows from other facts)
a node test and a live run each show a hand-back with the three kinds, rendered with the kind named on each item

A fact may name the facts it is based on (a based_on list of fact ids); the harness checks the ids exist, refuses a cycle, checks facts in dependency order, and when a fact fails it flags and drops every fact based on it, naming the failed fact as the reason
a replay in which fact f1 fails and f2, f3 name f1 in based_on drops all three, and the message to the model names f1 as the reason for f2 and f3; a cycle f1->f2->f1 is refused with the fix
A fact whose check is 'llm' is sent to the decider with the value and the cited result; the answer shows the decider's option beside it, and it is never counted with the facts a direct check passed
report.json counts direct-passed, llm-judged and derived facts separately, and the wording test finds none of them called accuracy
The strict behaviour is on for worker and cortex by default in the contract, with a per-run switch to turn it off for comparison arms
one recorded live run each on worker and cortex with the default contract shows dropped items in the walk and in the message the model received

The model's final reply, which associate run --json returns as final_reply and delegate_status passes to a peer (tools/delegate.ts:541), is labelled unchecked in every place it is returned, and the checked answer is returned beside it; the strict answer is not the only output a caller sees, so the label travels with the text
a test over associate run --json and delegate_status output finds final_reply only under a field or label that says unchecked, with the checked answer beside it

When the decider cannot be reached or gives a malformed answer, an llm or derived fact is not dropped as failed: it is kept out of the answer under its own label (not judged, with the reason) and the model is told; a run never loses items silently because of an outage
a fault-injected run with the decider unreachable keeps every llm and derived fact in the export under 'not judged', drops none as failed, and the message to the model names the outage

The number check and the printed result read the saved result file; when that file was cut at the contract cap (lib/results.ts:18) and the number or quote is not in the kept part, the fact is reported as not checkable from the saved result, with the fix to cite a narrower call
a replay with a saved result cut at the cap and a number beyond the cut reports the fact as not checkable from the saved result, with the fix

A fact that cites a prior run or a child (prior:wN, cN:wN) shows that run's command and result when the labelled export is available, and is otherwise marked as resting on a labelled run whose result was not read here; it is never shown as directly checked
a continued run citing prior:wN renders the prior call's command and result when the prior export is present, and the labelled-run wording when it is not; both are tests

The command printed in an answer is the recorded arguments with absolute paths under the checkout shown relative to it, and nothing from the environment; a test shows no home-directory path and no bearer value can appear in a rendered answer
a test renders an answer from a walk whose arguments hold an absolute worktree path and an environment-looking token, and the output holds neither

Every dropped item is kept in the export with its reason, the answer states how many items were dropped and for which reasons, and the run result carries those counts, so an answer that lost most of its items is visible as such
the measured colleague run in which no fact passed, replayed, renders an answer that states how many items were dropped and why, and the run result carries the same counts

The derived-fact question to the decider (does the conclusion follow from the listed facts) is tried on a labelled set before it decides drops, as the support question was; until then a derived fact is shown with the decider's answer and is dropped only when one of its inputs fails
a committed labelled set of derived facts with two raters, at least one not a Claude model, and the decider's answers on it, exists before the derived answer decides a drop
The measurement arm for strict facts grades what a caller receives: the rendered answer and, separately, the final reply; and it reports run time and the number of retry rounds per run
the broad report for the strict arm prints, per run, graded statements of the answer and of the final reply separately, the run time and the retry rounds used

The change is a contract event: accuracy.json and facts.schema.json get a version bump, exports written before it still load in associate check, and the Python re-check implements the same kinds, order and drops as the extension, with a parity test over shared fixtures

associate check loads a stored export written before the bump and one written after, and the parity test gives the same kinds, order and drops from the extension and the Python re-check on the shared fixtures

A model cannot lower the bar by its choice of kind: a fact whose cited call's result contains its quote or number is checked directly whatever kind it states, and the report counts how many facts of each kind a run used
a replay where a fact states kind llm and its quote is in the cited result is checked by the matcher and counted as direct, and report.json lists facts per kind

The model does not retype evidence. A fact names the call it rests on (walk id) and where in that call's saved result the evidence is (line range or search term); the harness copies the quoted text, the command as used and the result file into the fact by code. For a direct fact whose value is itself in the result (a count, a line, a match), the harness also takes the value from the result. The model writes only the claim wording for llm and derived facts, and those are judged against the evidence the harness copied. A fact whose pointer resolves to nothing is dropped with that reason.

In a recorded run, every quote and command shown in the answer is byte-for-byte what the saved result and the walk entry hold, and a fact whose pointer names lines past the end of the result is dropped with that reason; a test feeds a wrong pointer and sees the drop

tasks.summary: Contract: fact schema and accuracy settings for strict facts, with a version bump
acceptance_criteria: facts.schema.json accepts on a fact: kind (direct, llm, derived), at (a line range or a search term in the cited call's saved result), based_on (list of fact ids); quote becomes optional and value is optional for a direct fact; a schema version field is added

accuracy.json version is 2 and holds a strict block: on for worker and cortex, off for senses and super-vl, kept-with-a-mark answers (part, little), dropping answers (none), derived_decides_drops false
associate/contract/validate.py accepts the new files and refuses an unknown kind; pytest covers both; a fact written in the old shape (value, source, quote) still validates
tasks.instruction: Files: associate/contract/schemas/facts.schema.json, associate/contract/accuracy.json, associate/contract/validate.py, tests/test_contract*.py. Change no gate.json. Senses stays off (spec c29).

tasks.summary: Extension: resolve a fact's pointer and copy its evidence by code
acceptance_criteria: new lib/evidence.ts: given a fact's source and at, returns the quoted text copied from the saved result, the command built from the walk entry's args_used, and the result file name; for a direct fact with no value, the value is the copied text
a pointer that names lines past the end, or a search term not in the result, gives a named failure reason; a node test feeds each and sees it
a number in a fact's value is looked up in the copied result; absent gives a named reason
a saved result cut at the contract cap with the evidence beyond the cut gives 'not checkable from the saved result' with the fix to cite a narrower call
prior:wN and cN:wN sources resolve when the labelled export is present and otherwise give the labelled-run wording, never 'direct'

printed commands show paths under the checkout as relative and carry nothing from the environment; a node test with an absolute worktree path and a token-looking value in args_used finds neither in the output
a node test shows resolving starts no process and makes no tool call
a node test where the model's description of the command differs from args_used renders the args_used command
tasks.instruction: Files: new .pi/extensions/associate/lib/evidence.ts and .pi/extensions/associate/tests/evidence.test.ts only. Read lib/walk.ts (args_used), lib/results.ts (cap), lib/facts.ts (label lookup), lib/matcher.ts. Do not edit lib/facts.ts in this task.

tasks.summary: Extension: fact kinds, the kind floor, and the based_on graph
acceptance_criteria: lib/facts.ts reads kind and based_on; based_on ids must exist; a cycle is refused with the fix; facts are checked in dependency order

when a fact fails, every fact based on it (directly or through others) is flagged and dropped with the failed fact's id as the reason; node test: f1 fails, f2 and f3 name f1, all three drop and the message names f1 for f2 and f3; cycle f1 to f2 to f1 is refused
a fact stating kind llm or derived whose evidence is found by the direct check is checked directly and counted as direct; node test
check.json records each fact's stated kind, the kind it was checked as, and its drop reason
tasks.instruction: Files: .pi/extensions/associate/lib/facts.ts and its test file. Keep old-shape facts (quote, no kind) working as kind direct checked by the matcher.

tasks.summary: Extension: the decider judges llm and derived facts, and an outage is 'not judged'
acceptance_criteria: an llm fact is sent to the decider with its value and the evidence the harness copied, using the five-option support question; the option is stored on the fact

a derived fact is sent with its conclusion and the values of the facts it lists, asking whether the conclusion follows; the answer is stored and shown, and by contract (derived_decides_drops false) it never drops the fact

decider unreachable or malformed answer: the fact is marked not judged with the reason, is not dropped as failed, and the message to the model names the outage; node test with a fake decider that fails
llm-judged and derived facts are never counted with direct-passed facts
tasks.instruction: Files: .pi/extensions/associate/lib/support.ts plus a new .pi/extensions/associate/lib/judge.ts and tests. The derived question text goes in accuracy.json beside the support question (coordinate the key name with t1: strict.derived_question).

acceptance_criteria: with strict on: a fact that fails a direct check or is answered none is dropped; a fact answered part or little is returned once with the answer and the fix, and if still part or little it is kept with the mark 'evidence shows part of the value'
the model is told each dropped or returned item and why, and may answer again for retry_rounds; after the last round the answer goes out without the dropped items and the run is not refused

ASSOCIATE_STRICT (on or off) overrides the contract for one run; any other value is ignored with one stderr line; with strict off the present report/enforce behaviour is unchanged (existing node tests pass unmodified)
node tests cover: drop on none, return-then-keep on part, cascade message, rounds exhausted
tasks.instruction: Files: .pi/extensions/associate/lib/handback.ts, .pi/extensions/associate/tools/finish (where finish is registered), tests. Spec c28: no refusal after the last round in strict mode.

tasks.summary: Extension: render the answer from passed items only, with how to check each
acceptance_criteria: answer.md's answer section holds only items that passed or are kept with a mark; each shows its kind, the command, the result file and the copied evidence; an llm or derived item shows the decider's option
no sentence of the model's summary or final message is in the answer section; both stay in the export under the unchecked label
the answer states how many items were dropped, by reason; every dropped item is in the export with its reason
report.json counts direct-passed, llm-judged, derived, kept-with-mark, not-judged and dropped facts separately, and facts per stated kind
tasks.instruction: Files: .pi/extensions/associate/lib/render.ts and tests. Use the words 'quote found', 'checked', 'judged'; never 'accuracy' or 'score'.

associate check loads a stored export written before the bump and one written after

associate run --json carries the strict counts and the drop reasons; final_reply appears only under a field named as unchecked, with the checked answer beside it; delegate_status returns the same labelled pair; tests on both outputs

risks.text: Honesty condition h5 still says a returned fact 'narrows the value or the run ends refused'; c10 and c28 as amended say the fact is kept with a mark and the run is not refused. The plan follows c10 and c28; h5 should be reworded in the spec

risks.text: Whether models respond to drops by handing back fewer facts (spec park), how children and delegated runs behave under strict, and the time cost of retries are not known until t12 and t13

Only one review run by cortex has been measured before; its findings are a second opinion the main session checks, and each review run is recorded as one run, not a rate
